mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers discount rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS trend and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 0.5% per annum signals monetary tightening that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5%, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate and decline in non-farm payrolls signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of rising UNRATE and falling PAYEMS fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression has a p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts below 1500 thousand units signals cooling residential construction activity that reduces consumer confidence and corporate revenue expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days during a housing cycle peak.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST falls below 1500 during a housing cycle peak, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production growth indicates expanding economic output and corporate profitability, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO growth is positive, or the correlation between INDPRO growth and SPX returns is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 5.0% signals labor market stress that reduces household income and consumption, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 275) and accommodative monetary policy (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) signals elevated risk of future rate hikes, increasing market volatility and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of CPIAUCSL > 275 and FEDFUNDS < 0.5% fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression has a p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion, a slowdown in quarterly GDP growth below 2.0% signals an impending economic deceleration that reduces corporate earnings growth expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth falls below 2.0% during late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.
